slides.title: 7 Little Laws Smart People _Quietly_ Follow
slides.sub: Save these. You'll use them every week.

slides.title: Kidlin's Law
body: **Write a problem down clearly, and it's half solved.**
In your head, a worry is fog. On paper it becomes *a task with a first step.*

slides.title: Pareto's Law

graphic.q: Which 2 of your 10 tasks are the gold ones?

body: **Roughly 80% of results come from 20% of the effort.** It's a rule of thumb, not an exact law.
Find your gold 20% and *do it first.*

slides.title: Murphy's Law

graphic.note: Plan for it once. Then stop worrying about it.

body: **Anything that can go wrong, will.** That's not a reason to panic. It's a reason to prepare.
Spend 5 minutes listing what could break, and *give each one a plan.*

slides.title: Wilson's Law

graphic.q: Keep building. The money tends to catch up.

body: **Put knowledge first, and money tends to follow.**
Skills compound quietly, but the pay often *arrives later* than the effort. Most people quit in the gap.

slides.title: Gilbert's Law

graphic.prompt: Boss: “Can you sort out the client report?”

options.t: Propose the best way, then do it

graphic.q: Which one gets trusted with more?

body: **Nobody will tell you exactly what to do.** Working out the best way is part of the job.

slides.title: Falkland's Law
body: **When you don't have to decide, don't.**
Rushing adds pressure and mistakes. If the clock allows it, *waiting is a decision too.*

slides.title: Hick's Law

graphic.q: How many tabs do you have open right now?

body: **The more options you have, the longer it takes to choose.**
Shrink the menu. *Fewer choices* means faster, more confident decisions.

slides.title: Which One Do You Break Most?

graphic.q: Which of the 7 laws do you break most often?

body: Pick one law and use it this week. **Small rules, big difference.**
Save this, and share it with someone who needs it. *visualgrowth.app*
